docs.title: Society Protocol Web3 Outpost
docs.text: The Web3 Outpost is an Ethereum-based launchpad designed to preserve community alignment, maintain censorship-resistant accounts, and track verified contribution histories. It serves as a Schelling point bridging humanity from Web3 and Nation States into the Web4 Synchronized Era.

docs.title: Documentation Structure
docs.text:
This documentation is organized into six primary sections:

  • Concepts: The architectural principles of Society Protocol, codebase vs. instances, and how Genesis Energy is distributed.
  • Governance: The meritocratic DAO structure, Governor badges, and parallel feedback for SPEC holders.
  • Badges: The identity primitive of the Outpost, including permissions, badge standards, and partner tiers.
  • SPEC Token: Tokenomics, supply distribution, and the mechanics of locking tokens for VIP communication channels.
  • Guides: Step-by-step tutorials for creating accounts, minting badges, and interacting with the protocol.
  • Technical: Smart contract addresses, proxy architectures, and the Badge ID registry for developers and auditors.

docs.title: SPEC Token: Objective Contribution & Economics
docs.text: The SPEC Token is the objective contribution storage token of the Society Protocol movement. It works alongside the account system to provide a real-time, sybil-resistant community map on Ethereum.

docs.title: Subjective vs. Objective Contribution
docs.text:
To understand how the Web3 Outpost enables the launching of Web4 Society Protocol (SP) instances, contributions are separated into two distinct layers:

Layer System Role in Web4 Genesis Example Subjective Contribution Accounts & Badges (ERC-1155) Determines WHO gets invited as Genesis Actors "Invite accounts with Builder Badge" Objective Contribution SPEC Token (ERC-20) Determines HOW MUCH Energy each account receives "Allocate Energy proportional to SPEC balance"

Together, Subjective Accounts and Objective SPEC holdings form a sybil-resistant community map. Upstart SP instances use this map to launch cohesive, legitimate instances populated by interested participants at scale.

docs.title: Use Cases of the SPEC Token
1. Primary Use Case: Genesis Energy Allocation (~75 Year Horizon)
docs.text: The primary function of SPEC is to be held as stored contribution value. Upstart Web4 SP instances recognize SPEC token holdings to allocate initial Energy distributions to legitimate participants. The Web3 Outpost remains active and valuable for decades to facilitate this launchpad transition.

docs.title: 2. VIP Rooms (Gold, Silver, Bronze)
docs.text: Users lock SPEC tokens to enter exclusive, spam-free VIP communication channels. This allows committed participants to form long-term relationships and strategic partnerships.

docs.title: 3. Liquidity Provision (LP Rewards)
docs.text: 5% of the total SPEC supply (500,000,000 SPEC) is earmarked for liquidity providers in the SPEC/WETH pool, distributed evenly over a 5-year period.

docs.title: Governance Role: Parallel Feedback (Non-Voting)
docs.text:
To prevent sybil attacks and economic treasury capture (which plague traditional Web3 token-voting DAOs), SPEC is not used for direct execution voting in the SP DAO.

  • Meritocratic Governance: Execution decisions are made exclusively by Governor Badges held by accountable core team members, advisors, and partner communities.
  • Community Parallel Feedback: SPEC token holders can run parallel feedback votes on governance proposals. Governors review this feedback to gauge broader community sentiment before executing decisions.
  • Modular Decision Delegation: In the future, Governors may delegate specific modular decision-making power to SPEC holders on a per-decision basis.

docs.title: Overview & Access Mechanics
docs.text: Acquire VIP Badges by locking SPEC tokens (0x6AcD...18BA) in protocol vaults. By requiring a time-bound token lockup, the protocol makes sybil manipulation economically unviable, keeping VIP channels highly aligned.

docs.title: Community & Contributor Badges
docs.text: This page covers official badges awarded to individual community members, active contributors, early financial backers, and creative competition winners across the Society Protocol ecosystem.

docs.title: Contributor Badge (ID: 26)
docs.text:
The Contributor Badge is awarded to dedicated community members who actively contribute to the Society Protocol movement through research, content, organizing, ecosystem support, or technical initiatives.

Rather than requiring full-time software engineering, this badge recognizes high levels of alignment, consistent engagement, and meaningful effort in helping the protocol grow.

docs.title: Purpose & Discord Access
docs.text:
A primary utility of the Contributor Badge is granting access to an exclusive, token-gated channel in the official Society Protocol Discord.

The goal of this channel is to cultivate a focused, low-noise environment for higher-level discussion, strategic feedback, and direct coordination with core contributors and ambassadors without the clutter of public channels.

docs.title: How to Unlock the Private Discord Channel
docs.text:
If you hold a Contributor Badge in your wallet, you can claim your role in Discord using the Collab.Land bot:

  1. Join the Discord: Make sure you are in the official Society Protocol Discord server.
  2. Locate the Verification Channel: Navigate to #collabland-join (or #role-verify).
  3. Connect Your Wallet: Click on the "Let's go!" button provided by the official Collab.Land bot.
  4. Sign the Message: Follow the unique link to open the Collab.Land interface in your browser and connect the Ethereum wallet that holds your Contributor Badge. Sign the gasless signature to prove ownership.
  5. Access Granted: Once verified, Collab.Land automatically grants you the @Contributor role in Discord, unlocking access to the private contributor channel immediately.

[!NOTE] The Contributor Badge is Soulbound (non-transferable). Only the wallet address that originally received the badge can claim the Discord role.

docs.title: Early Backers: ICO Participant Badge (ID: 27)
docs.text:
The ICO Participant Badge honors early financial supporters who participated in the initial SPEC token fundraiser event (Dutch auction).

  • Badge ID: 27
  • Transferability: Soulbound
  • Perks & Significance:
    • Provides permanent on-chain proof of early belief and capital commitment to the Society Protocol vision from Day 1.
    • Serves as a key historical credential queried by future Web4 SP instances to grant starting Genesis Energy bonuses to founding community backers.

docs.title: Community Awards & Contests
docs.text: Society Protocol regularly hosts community competitions, bounties, and creative hackathons to showcase community talent.

docs.title: Creative Contest Winner Badge
docs.text:
The Creative Contest Winner Badge is an official recognition badge awarded to participants who win or place in community creative initiatives, including:

  • Visual design, art, and meme competitions
  • Community writing and deep-dive article contests
  • Video essays, animations, and educational media

This badge stands as a permanent tribute in your Outpost profile, verifying your creative contribution to the culture and lore of Society Protocol.

docs.title: Community Partners
docs.text: Partner communities commit to the Society Protocol movement's ideology in exchange for official recognition, UI feature prioritization, and tier badges on the Web3 Outpost.

docs.title: What is a Community Partner?
docs.text:
Society Protocol is designed to foster a decentralized federation of aligned groups, projects, and network state experiments. A Community Partner is an established Web3 community, DAO, or organization that has formally aligned with the Society Protocol movement.

Rather than operating in isolation, partner communities deploy badges on the Outpost, coordinate shared initiatives, and establish early relationships that will carry forward into upstart Web4 instances.

docs.title: Partner Community Tiers
docs.text:
Partnership tiers reflect levels of organizational integration, collaborative depth, and ecosystem commitment:

Tier Badge Recognition & Perks Tier 1 Gold Partner Badge Top-tier partner communities. Receive direct feature feedback pipelines with the core development team and full Web3 Outpost UI enclave integration. Tier 2 Silver Partner Badge Mid-tier partner communities with specialized working group affiliation and joint research / governance initiatives. Tier 3 Bronze Partner Badge Formally associated community partners recognized across the Outpost ecosystem.

docs.title: Role in Web4 Genesis Instances
docs.text: When independent Web4 Society Protocol instances launch in the future, founders can query the Web3 Outpost to invite partner community members directly as founding actors, granting them starting Energy or specialized rights based on their verified community partner affiliation.

docs.title: Badges Overview & Permissions
docs.text: Society Protocol badges are categorized into Official Badges (issued by the SP DAO) and Community Badges (created by partner protocols and community admins through the Outpost interface).

docs.title: Meritocratic DAO vs. SPEC Holders
docs.text:
A critical design principle of Society Protocol is the separation between meritocratic governance and economic contribution:

  • DAO Governors (Governor Badges): The SP DAO is a meritocracy governed by accountable core team members, strategic advisors, and partner communities holding Governor Badges. It explicitly avoids pseudonymous token-based voting to prevent sybil attacks and treasury capture.
  • SPEC Token Holders: SPEC holders participate in economic alignment, VIP channels, and community feedback polls, while qualifying for Genesis Energy distributions in Web4 instances.

docs.title: The 4 ERC-1155 Permissions Explained
docs.text: Permissions control who can issue, destroy, move, or configure badges within the system:

docs.title: 1. Mint Permission
docs.text:
• Definition: The authority to create new instances of a specific Badge ID and assign them to recipient addresses.
  • Official Badges: Held by the SP DAO Safe (0xdfdC...7579) or automated hooks (e.g. zkTLS verification or SPEC locking vaults).
  • Community Badges: Held by the community's admin address.

docs.title: 2. Burn Permission
docs.text:
• Definition: The authority to destroy existing badges from an account.
  • Official Badges: Restricted to self-burn by the holder or revocation by the Security Council Safe (0xCc4F...98AC) during operational offboarding.
  • Community Badges: Configured by the community admin.

docs.title: 3. Transfer Permission
docs.text:
• Definition: The ability to transfer a badge between accounts.
  • Official Badges: Most official badges are Soulbound (Transfer disabled) to preserve credential integrity. VIP Badges follow SPEC lockup rules.
  • Community Badges: Configurable upon creation.

docs.title: 4. Manage Permission
docs.text:
• Definition: Admin control over badge metadata URIs, royalties, and hook attachments.
  • Official Badges: Governed by the SP DAO Safe.
  • Community Badges: Managed by the community admin via the Community Registry (0xEa00...EB76).

docs.title: Accounts & Badges
docs.text:
In Web3, a wallet is just a cryptographic key. It has no history, no reputation, and no identity. Anyone can create a thousand wallets in a minute.

The Web3 Outpost solves this by introducing Accounts and Badges. This is the core identity primitive of the Outpost, it transforms an anonymous wallet into a recognizable participant with a verifiable history.

docs.title: Accounts
docs.text:
All participants in the Society Protocol movement create an Ethereum-based account within the Web3 Outpost.

  • Long-Term Continuity: Users are encouraged to maintain a single main account. While anyone can create a new wallet, the Outpost rewards those who maintain a single account that accumulates a rich, multi-year history of contributions and relationships.

docs.title: What is a Badge?
docs.text:
Badges are verifiable digital credentials minted directly to your account. They serve two primary roles:

  1. Functional Credentials: They act as keys. A specific badge might unlock a private Discord channel, grant voting rights in the DAO, or give you admin moderation powers.
  2. Permanent Attributions: They act as a resume. They create verifiable proof of event attendance, core code contributions, or verified off-chain attributes (like proving you hold a specific passport without revealing your identity).

docs.title: Why ERC-1155?
docs.text:
You will often see badges referred to as ERC-1155 tokens. Here is why that matters.

In crypto, there are different "standards" for tokens:

  • ERC-20 is like a standard dollar bill. Every dollar is identical and interchangeable.
  • ERC-721 is like a unique painting. There is only one, and it cannot be replaced.
  • ERC-1155 is like a digital ticket wallet. It allows a single smart contract to manage both unique items (a one-of-a-kind VIP pass) and multi-copy items (10,000 general admission tickets) at the same time.

For the Outpost, ERC-1155 is perfect. It allows us to issue thousands of "Builder" badges (multi-copy) and a single "Security Council" badge (unique) using the same system, which saves massive amounts of gas fees and keeps the architecture clean.

docs.title: How Badges are Issued (The Verification Mechanism)
docs.text:
Issuing a badge is not a manual process. The Outpost uses automated smart contracts (known as Hooks) to ensure badges cannot be forged or duplicated.

  1. The Verification: When you claim a badge, the Outpost verifies your eligibility. This can happen in two ways:

    • zkTLS: You cryptographically prove an off-chain fact (e.g., "I own this GitHub account" or "I am a verified Argentine citizen") without revealing your passwords or personal data.
    • SPEC Lockup: You lock SPEC tokens in a vault to prove economic commitment.

  2. The Hook: Once verified, a smart contract (the Hook) automatically approves the transaction. It ensures you haven't already claimed the badge (preventing duplicates).

  3. The Mint: The badge is minted to your account. Most governance and role badges are Soulbound, meaning they are permanently locked to your account and cannot be transferred or sold to someone else.

Note that, the Web3 Outpost provide the freedom to the communities to determine the way they want to configure their own badges.

docs.title: Codebase vs. Instances
docs.text: Society Protocol operates under an organizational and architectural framework similar to the Linux Foundation.

docs.title: A Single Codebase, Many Communities
docs.text:
Civilization only needs one impeccably secure, highly modular, and credibly neutral codebase for Society Protocol to spawn an infinite number of customizable instances.

                  +-----------------------------------+
                  |   SOCIETY PROTOCOL CORE CODEBASE  |
                  |   (Secure, Modular, Neutral)      |
                  +-----------------------------------+
                                    |
          +-------------------------+-------------------------+
          |                         |                         |
          v                         v                         v
+-------------------+     +-------------------+     +-------------------+
|  SP Instance #1   |     |  SP Instance #2   |     |  SP Instance #3   |
| (Eco-Community)   |     | (Network State)   |     | (DeFi Guild)      |
| Custom Parameters |     | Custom Parameters |     | Custom Parameters |
+-------------------+     +-------------------+     +-------------------+

docs.title: The Linux Analogy
docs.text:
• The Core Codebase (Linux Kernel): Maintained by the Society Protocol organization. It provides the minimal-viable-product (MVP) state transition functions (STF), Energy state machine, account abstractions, and core Value Functions (VFs).
  • SP Instances (Linux Distributions): Independent deployments created by communities, DAOs, or nation-states. Each instance configures its own Value Functions, Constitutions, UIs, and initial Energy distributions.

docs.title: The Three Core Principles
docs.text:
To allow thousands of diverse communities to trust and adopt Society Protocol, the core codebase adheres strictly to three principles:

  1. Impeccable Security: Entrusting human identity and society to a state machine carries immense responsibility. The core layers undergo rigorous battle-testing and concentric audit rings.
  2. Modular Architecture: Communities configure distinct Value Functions without altering core security.
  3. Credible Neutrality: The stewards of the codebase remain strictly neutral. The core team does not start or rule SP instances; it builds the generic, fair infrastructure for all instances to bloom.

docs.title: Genesis Energy
docs.text: One of the most valuable aspects of participating in the Web3 Outpost is qualifying for Genesis Energy Distributions across newly spawned Society Protocol instances over decades.

docs.title: What is Genesis Energy?
docs.text:
In Web4 Society Protocol instances, Energy is the foundational resource unit used to measure economic output, governance weight, and systemic participation within Synchronized States.

When an SP instance launches:

  • It requires a legitimate initial distribution of Energy among its founding accounts.
  • Manually picking accounts and manually deciding Energy amounts creates severe political conflict and coordination bottlenecks.
  • The Web3 Outpost solution: Upstart instances query the Web3 Outpost to identify verified accounts (Subjective Map via Badges) and distribute initial Energy proportional to SPEC Token holdings (Objective Map).

docs.text:
+-------------------------------+
                       |   WEB3 OUTPOST SPEC HOLDINGS  |
                       +-------------------------------+
                                       |
    +----------------------------------+----------------------------------+
    |                                  |                                  |
    v                                  v                                  v
+------------------------+ +------------------------+ +------------------------+
| SP Instance A (2029)   | | SP Instance B (2032)   | | SP Instance C (2040)   |
| Energy Airdrop to SPEC | | Energy Airdrop to SPEC | | Energy Airdrop to SPEC |
+------------------------+ +------------------------+ +------------------------+

Over the next 20 to 70 years, millions of SP instances are expected to be launched by startup communities, DAOs, networks, and nation-states.

Holding SPEC tokens and building an account history in the Web3 Outpost provides participants with the potential for continuous Genesis Energy airdrops across thousands of independent SP instances over decades.

docs.title: Why Instances Choose SPEC for Energy Distribution
docs.text:
Upstart SP instances are not forced to grant SPEC holders Energy, but incentives naturally align:

  1. Legitimacy & Sybil-Resistance: SPEC token holdings represent authentic historical skin-in-the-game.
  2. Attracting Active Participants: Granting Energy to SPEC holders attracts an experienced, highly aligned base of early adopters.
  3. Automated Scale: Using SPEC and Badges eliminates manual invite negotiations, enabling instances to launch at scale on day one.

docs.title: Governance & the SP DAO
docs.text: The Society Protocol movement is not a democracy; it is a meritocracy. Governance is designed to compress the highest and most aligned expertise possible—from our core team and deeply experienced affiliates—to make aligned, optimal group decisions while bypassing the sybil-vulnerabilities of traditional Web3 token-voting.

docs.title: Meritocratic Architecture
docs.text:
The Society Protocol DAO serves as the decision-making body and treasury for the movement:

  • Governed Exclusively by Governors: The DAO is governed by holders of the Governor Badge (ID: 13)—meritocratically appointed members from the core team and affiliates (strategic advisors and partner communities) who possess specialized expertise and direct skin in the game.
  • Exclusion of Pseudonymous Accounts & SPEC: Unlike typical token-based DAOs, pseudonymous accounts and raw SPEC token holdings are deliberately excluded from direct execution voting. This prevents economic treasury capture, plutocracy, and sybil manipulation.
  • Accountable Peer Management: Governors may add or remove peers based on proven contributions and alignment, ensuring decision-making power remains with identifiable, accountable stewards.

docs.title: The Role of SPEC Holders: Parallel Feedback
docs.text:
While the SPEC token does not confer direct executive voting power, community perspective is vital:

  • Snapshot Parallel Feedback Space: SPEC token holders can vote on proposals in a parallel decision-making structure via Snapshot.
  • Sentiment & Mindset Gauge: This space gives Governors direct, unfiltered insight into community sentiment, perceptions, and intentions without encumbering token holders with the operational and legal overhead of protocol execution.
  • Modular Decision Delegation: In future phases, Governors may elect to delegate specific modular decision-making power to SPEC holders on a per-decision basis.

docs.text:

Community-Level Governance: The governance documented above applies strictly to the global Society Protocol DAO. Individual communities hosted on the Outpost configure their own internal decision-making frameworks within their specific community dashboard at app.societyprotocol.io/communities.

docs.title: Create a Personal Account
docs.text: You need to have an account in the Web3 Outpost to interact with the protocol.

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: Connect your wallet (create one if needed) and visit https://app.societyprotocol.io/ Click on "Connect Wallet" in the top-right corner to start the sign-up process.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: Once your wallet is connected go to the left sidebar and click on "Accounts". Then click on "Setup Account" and follow the procedure.

docs.title: Create a Badge
docs.text: This guide explains how to deploy custom ERC-1155 badges using the Web3 Outpost interface.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: You need to have a personal account in the Web3 Outpost.

docs.title: Step-by-Step Guide
docs.text: Once you mint your Identity, you can go to the badge section on the left side and start the process of badge creation.

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: Connect the same wallet you used the for the account creation. Click on the left sidebar "Badges" section.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: Enter the name of the badge and the badge image use to represent the badge. The metadata sections allows you to fit additional information about the badge.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Once you finish with the name and image, click the button "Next"

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: On this section you can define the following permissions: "Mint", "Burn", "Transfer" and who can "Manage" the badge. This is really customizable and it allows for all kinds of combinations depending the specific usage you want to give it.

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: You can watch your Badges on the "Individual" section as well as in the toogle "Managed by Me".

docs.title: Create a Community Badge
docs.text: This tutorial will guide you through the process of creating a custom badge for your community on the Web3 Outpost.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
You need to have a community in the Web3 Outpost, and the administrative rights to your community dashboard.

Step-by-Step:

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: Access to you community dashboard and go to the "Badges" toogle.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: Click the button "Create Badge".

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Enter the details of the badge. Name, image and metadata.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: On this section you can define the following permissions: "Mint", "Burn", "Transfer" and who can "Manage" the badge. This is really customizable and it allows for all kinds of combinations depending the specific usage you want to give it .

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Double check the best configuration for your usecase and click on "Finish".

docs.title: Create a Community
docs.text: This tutorial will guide you through the process of creating a community within the Web3 Outpost.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: You need to have a personal account in the Web3 Outpost.

docs.title: Step-by-Step Guide
docs.text: Once you mint your Identity, you can go to the badge section on the left side and start the process of badge creation.

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: Go to the "Communities" section on the left sidebar. Click on "Create Community"button on the top-right corner.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: Fill in your community creation name and description. Click Next.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: You get the Manager Badge an can customized additional data on the metadata section. Add an image for the Assistant Badge and the Member Badge so people can differentiate them in the badge list. Click Next.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: The member badge will be your most used badge, so make sure it is well represented.

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Double check you finish setting up all the metadata and click "Create".

docs.title: Step 6
docs.text: Click "Finish" and sign all the required transactions to validate the action. The process can take a few minutes depending on the network conditions.

docs.title: Step 7
docs.text: If the transaction went through, you will see the following message: "Community Created!". You can view now the community on the web3 outpost or in Etherscan.

docs.title: Step 8
docs.text: You now have a dashboard where all the actions related to you community get logged. You can see members, badge and future features we will add in the future.

docs.title: Add Community Members
docs.text:
The way we add community members to our communities is by minting them a Community Member Badge.

This guide explains how to complete the minting process for single persons or a group of people.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: The people you want to add must have an account in the Web3 Outpost. You also need Manager permissions on the community to mint badges.

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: Go to your Community dashboard and select the "Members" toogle.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: In the right side you will find the column for Actions. You can Mint and Burn in this section. In the Badge selection choose the badge you want to mint. In this case we will use the Member Badge since we want to start getting people into our community.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: The recipient adress section will display a full list of addresses who have an account inside the web3 Outpost. This list is filterable and searchable. If you found the person you want to assign that badge select him and click the button "Mint Badge".

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: In case you want to Mint your member badge in a batch then just select that option and upload a CSV file with all the adress you want to add. (Again, those adresses must have an account in the Web3 Outpost to receive the badge and follow the format explained on the Web3 Outpost).

docs.title: Architectural Overview
docs.text:
1. ERC-1967 Proxies: Core contracts (SocietyProtocolBadges, CommunityWrapperFactory, CommunityRegistry) use transparent proxies. Integrations interact exclusively with proxy addresses.

  2. Multisig Safes: Treasury and contract upgrades are managed by the SP DAO Safe (0xdfdC...7579). Emergency circuit breakers are managed by the Security Council Safe (0xCc4F...98AC).

  3. Hooks: SingleMintHook (0xc5cA...FC6D) enforces strict single-token limits per account for soulbound badges.
